question: the Calderon 2022 tables for the fly test: what was fetched, its size, hash and licence
source: Calderon D, Blecher-Gonen R, Huang X, Secchia S, Kentro J, Daza RM, Martin B, Dulja A, Schaub C, Trapnell C, Larschan E, O'Connor-Giles KM, Furlong EEM, Shendure J (2022) The continuum of Drosophila embryonic development at single-cell resolution. Science 377:eabn5800, doi:10.1126/science.abn5800; supplementary tables, peak set and cell annotations from the authors' site (DEAP), RNA counts from GEO GSE190147

fetched.what: Calderon 2022 supplementary tables S1-S13; read: TableS2 (ATAC cluster annotations) and TableS4 (ATAC marker accessible regions)
fetched.name: SupplementaryTables.xlsx
fetched.licence: not stated on the authors' site (DEAP); the article is Science 377:eabn5800

fetched.what: the full ATAC peak set, dm6
fetched.name: peaks.bed
fetched.licence: not stated on the authors' site (DEAP)

fetched.what: RNA cell identifiers to the annotations used in the source's Fig. 3 (manual_annot)
fetched.name: rna_meta.rds
fetched.licence: not stated on the authors' site (DEAP)

fetched.name: GSE190147_scirnaseq_gene_matrix.rows.txt.gz
fetched.licence: GEO public record; no licence stated by the submitters

fetched.what: RNA matrix column names (cells) with per-cell QC fields
fetched.name: GSE190147_scirnaseq_gene_matrix.columns.txt.gz
fetched.licence: GEO public record; no licence stated by the submitters

fetched.what: RNA UMI count matrix, genes x cells (MatrixMarket); summed by annotation, then deleted
fetched.name: GSE190147_scirnaseq_gene_matrix.mtx.gz
fetched.licence: GEO public record; no licence stated by the submitters

fetched.what: Ensembl 104 gene models for dm6 (BDGP6.32); its 13,968 protein-coding gene names all appear among the RNA matrix's row names
fetched.name: Drosophila_melanogaster.BDGP6.32.104.gff3.gz
fetched.licence: Ensembl states no restrictions on use of its data; the gene models are FlyBase's (CC BY 4.0)

distilled.what: UMI counts summed over cells by the source's manual_annot (rna_meta.rds), all windows pooled; one row per matrix row (gene name), one column per annotation

not_used.source: Calderon 2022 ATAC peak-by-cell matrices (DEAP ATAC/revision/peak_matrices; GEO GSE190130)
not_used.bytes: 119 MB to 2.1 GB per window and experiment, about 15 GB in all
not_used.why_not: over the 1.5 GB budget; Table S4 carries the source's own per-cluster call

not_used.source: Calderon 2022 ATAC bigWigs per window and cluster (DEAP ATAC/revision/bigwigs)
not_used.bytes: 2 MB to 577 MB each, more than 100 files
not_used.why_not: a per-element read of every cluster track would move most of each file

not_used.source: Measured insulator or TAD boundary sets (dCTCF, BEAF-32, CP190; embryo Hi-C)
not_used.why_not: the node decision (docs/SIMPLER-GENOMES.md section 8): this run replicates the worm's rule

sources.accession: Calderon D, Blecher-Gonen R, Huang X, Secchia S, Kentro J, Daza RM, Martin B, Dulja A, Schaub C, Trapnell C, Larschan E, O'Connor-Giles KM, Furlong EEM, Shendure J (2022) The continuum of Drosophila embryonic development at single-cell resolution. Science 377:eabn5800, doi:10.1126/science.abn5800; supplementary tables, peak set and cell annotations from the authors' site (DEAP), RNA counts from GEO GSE190147
sources.version: authors' site files as served on 2026-10-10; GEO GSE190147

sources.accession: Ensembl release 104, Drosophila melanogaster BDGP6.32 (dm6) GFF3

inputs.partition: the fetch record written by scripts/simpler_fly_fetch.py

result_manifest.assembly: dm6 (BDGP6.32): the peaks, the source's RNA alignment and the gene models; nothing is lifted

coordinates.note: the peaks are BED (0-based, half-open) and the GFF3 is 1-based closed; the element midpoint (start + end) // 2 moves by at most 1 bp between the two conventions

exclusions: the RNA matrix (697,773,156 bytes) was summed by annotation and deleted
result_manifest.partitions: n/a: an inventory has no evaluation partition

entry_script.why: argv[0] is a file inside this repository that git tracks and reports unmodified: the commit holds the code that wrote the bytes, so a rebuild can run it. The only clean form
entry_script.forms_are_decided_in_advance: genomeos.manifest.ENTRY_FORMS: one clean form (a tracked, unmodified file inside this repository), every other form refuses, and a form that cannot be classified is 'unknown' and refuses too. Read from sys.argv[0] at write time, never declared

code_cleanliness.counting_path_is_computed: the transitive import closure of this script, computed from the files' import statements at write time (genomeos.manifest.counting_path), never by importing: it follows every import that resolves to a file in this repository rather than only the package, counts the __init__.py of each package above a module, resolves bare imports against the directories the source literally puts on sys.path as well as the repository root, and matches every path component against what its directory lists, so a class name such as genomeos.genome.Genome cannot enter it as a file; not a hand-written list
code_cleanliness.note: several lanes work in this one checkout. A file under foreign_uncommitted_code belongs to another lane; this lane did not write it and did not commit it. The counting path is the computed closure above, so a foreign file outside it cannot have entered a number here, and foreign_uncommitted_code_on_the_counting_path names any that could

revision_stamps.sampled: code_cleanliness.git_sha is read while the writer computes; code.git_sha is read when the result is written. Both are HEAD of the same checkout at two moments
revision_stamps.reading: no revision race: both stamps record 67aff11

traced_inputs.note: Every file this writer opened for reading under data/ was recorded by an audit hook on the "open" event, canonicalised through data/'s links so one file has one spelling, and compared against the inputs the manifest declares; a member of a declared group counts as declared and hashed on its own, a file under a declared directory counts as declared by prefix. The hook is per interpreter, so a file read by a subprocess is not in this record, nor is one reached through a path that canonicalises to neither this checkout's data/ nor one of its link targets.
